_meta.paper: The Macroeconomic Limits of AI Compute
_meta.units: $B unless stated; rates per year; shares 0-1
_meta.rule: Each entry: value (triangular min/mode/max or scalar), source, source_date, next_update (when the source next publishes), trigger (what would move it), maps_to (model parameter).

capex_history.source: Epoch AI (2023-25); 2026 = Q2 guidance: GOOG 195-205, MSFT ~175 calendar, AMZN ~220, META 135-145, ORCL ~50

life_training.source: thermal physics (JEDEC JEP122, Llama-3 field data)

opex_share.source: decomposed: PUE, tariff (EIA), utilization, staff, tax, network
opex_share.flag: disputed input (v27): Goldman Sachs/Epoch use $836M per GW-yr non-D&A opex, ~2% of capital (power and maintenance only). Paper decomposition adds staffing, property tax/insurance, network, other = 6.65%. Gap ~$85-115B/yr of carry 2028-30. Adopting 0.02 would be a MATERIAL re-issue (|dz|>=0.5); not adopted pending a sourced operator cost per MW-year.

grid_cap.flag: high anchor (v27): Goldman Sachs semiconductor build implies 20/35/57 GW of AI deployments in 2026/27/28 (all buyers); 57 GW is above this range top (40 GW/yr). Observable to test in 2028 energization data.

reissue_rule.minor: any input change: rerun, update tables, bump version, no re-release
reissue_rule.material: |delta z_2030| >= 0.5 OR |delta g*_2030| >= 5 points OR P(profit 2030, rationalize) moves >= 15 points OR any 2026 observable outside its P10-P90 -> re-release with a delta log
reissue_rule.cadence: after each Big-5 earnings week (late Jan, late Apr, late Jul, late Oct) and after Nvidia (Feb/May/Aug/Nov)
